title: Manoeuvring against weaknesses

D0.outcome: Explains manoeuvring as purposeful regrouping against a weakness attackable in two ways, with a pivot through which pieces pass.

D1.outcome: In a given position, names the target, the pivot square and the route for each piece.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, chooses a regrouping that keeps more room for his pieces than the defender's, and avoids aimless moves.

D3.outcome: Predicts when the defender's variety of targets offsets a lack of variety of threats.

misconceptions: Manoeuvring is shuffling until the opponent errs.
conditions: A weakness attackable in at least two ways, more room for his forces, and a pivot.
contrasts: No pivot square exists, so the pieces cannot pass through one point.
A tactical position that needs no regrouping.
